ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1998A.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄): Dahui Zonggao is the exact headword speaker. Dahui describes the fear and responds by questioning whether the one who fears falling into blankness is itself empty. The exact headword-bearing actor is Dahui Zonggao. This exact quoted claim is anchored in the reviewed source unit.

Senses.Explanation: The records warn against collapsing into blank nothing, then answer that blankness itself is absent or is not blank. Literally, 'fall into emptiness,' but in these records the observable warning is against falling into a blank nothing. The term occurs 325 times in 128 allowed texts; the expanded form 'fall into blank annihilation' (落空亡) occurs 75 times in 43 texts. Dahui reports people who hear 'a teaching in which nothing is obtained' (無所得法) and become afraid that they will fall into blankness; he answers by asking whether the very one who fears falling into blankness is empty. A lamp dialogue answers the charge that Chan teachers mostly fall into blankness by saying that letters and other things arise from wisdom and that, when 'great function appears before one' (大用現前), there can be no falling into blankness. Another exchange dismantles the spatial wording itself: asked whether 'originally there is nothing' falls into blankness, the reply asks, 'Since blankness is absent, from where could falling be established?' (空既是無，墮從何立). The same collection says that people fear forgetting mind because they fear falling into blankness with nowhere to get hold, then says 'blankness itself is originally not blank' (空本無空). There are 6 occurrences of 'not fall into blankness' (不落空) and 21 of the warning 'do not fall into blankness' (莫落空).

Senses.Explanation: To fall into second place is the corpus verdict for something that may be valid or accomplished and yet is already secondary: even awakening, knowing, or accepting another person’s pointing can arrive one move late. Yangshan says awakening is not absent but falls into second place. Huitong Qingdan applies the verdict to awakening on hearing a saying; Feiyin gives it as the answer about the sentence after recognition; Yuanwu applies it to placing an eye before the first breath of things; Miyun applies it to needing another person’s pointing; Dahui criticizes teachers who make awakening itself secondary.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：福勝一片地，行也任你行，住也任你住。步步踏著，始知落處。若未然者，直須退步，脚下看取。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120) (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): Tianbo Chongyuan is the exact hall speaker, saying that only by treading the ground step after step does one know the landing place and otherwise must step back and look underfoot.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase asks or states the place where something comes down, settles, or finds its point of application. Chan exchanges use that ordinary landing-place relation to press where a saying, action, or person’s understanding actually comes to rest. Chan records apply it to words, answers, cases, actions, people, and one's life: 'know where it lands' (知落處) occurs 897 times in 226 files representing 223 independent works, while 'not know where it lands' (不知落處) occurs 209 times in 103 files representing 101 independent works. Yuanwu says that as soon as Danxia raised it, he knew where it landed (才方舉起便知落處), and his Blue Cliff prose twice contrasts knowing and not knowing where Mazu's public case lands. Dahui asks whether the assembly knows where his teacher's words land and says that knowing it identifies the top graduate (還知師翁落處麼。若知落處便識得狀元). Changqing asks, 'Do you understand where it lands?' (還委落處麼). A lamp record joins origin and destination: 'if you know where it arises, then you know where life lands' (若知起處。便知身命落處). Xiuyelin gives the richest explicit relation found: 'the fundamental matter is precisely where the person's own life-source lands' (本分事者，即當人本命元辰之落處也). The article therefore keeps the verbal image and reports what the texts assign a landing point; it does not replace that image with an imported abstraction.
